answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by binding each identity to a unique physical sensor on a remote island that must daily photograph a local sparrow and log a fresh quill-ink calibration mark under timed lighting. The signed reading is submitted on-chain. An attacker faking many identities must either ship and power dozens of real island sensors—costs that grow linearly with farm size—or face detection when correlated sparrow timings and identical sensor noise appear across accounts, since only one device can capture the true local events.
